clue.text: Minimal weight of octogenarian strippeuse?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a billionth of a gram, a tiny weight
second meaning, punning: a stripper-gram delivered by a nan (grandmother) would be a ...

explanation.walkthrough: The second half plays on novelty greetings such as the kissogram and strippogram: an elderly granny doing the job makes a NAN-O-GRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A nano- prefix means one billionth, so this unit is a billionth of a gram, a truly tiny mass.

clue.text: Root taking part in mixed doubles

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tennis player's roots in the game lie in playing mixed doubles.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddo is the edible tuber of the taro plant, a starchy tropical root vegetable.

clue.text: Youth recruited by special forces leaves

indicators.note: being recruited by a unit means being taken into it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: SAS is the Special Air Service, the British special forces regiment
a youth is a lad

explanation.surface: A young man is signed up by the special forces and then walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' reads as a verb, someone quitting, but it is a plural noun for salad greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes of mixed raw greens such as lettuce are made of leaves, so the plural noun fits.

clue.text: New designer loaded paint remover into shed

indicators.note: loaded means drunk, and the drunken letters are scrambled
the word into is shed, its letters taken out of the fodder before rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A decorator piles paint stripper into the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take PAINT REMOVER, shed the letters of INTO to leave PAREMVER, and 'loaded' rearranges those letters into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who revamps something gives it a fresh look, so they are a designer of a new version.

clue.text: Policemen supporting China's changing appearance

parts.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
to be for something is to support it
Ming is a famous dynasty of Chinese porcelain, so china here is Ming

explanation.surface: Police officers backing China while it changes its look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China's' looks like the country, but it is porcelain: MING ware.
explanation.definitionFit: To disform is to alter the shape or form of something, hence changing how it looks.

clue.text: Yellow-flowering shrub? Royal couple look skywards!

parts.note: K for king plus ER, Elizabeth Regina, make a royal pair

indicators.note: in a down entry, going skywards means read upwards, so the word is turned around

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: A king and queen gaze up at the sky beside a flowering bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerria is a Japanese rose shrub of the rose family, bearing bright golden blooms in spring.

clue.text: Maybe King willing one such as Napoleon …

parts.note: a king is one example of a playing card
game means willing, up for it

explanation.surface: A monarch is perhaps keen to emulate the French emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon looks like the emperor, which the puzzle's other answers play on, but here it is a trick-taking game played with cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon, or nap, is a trick-taking pastime played with a pack, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Dictator's use of unlawful force out …

indicators.note: a dictator here is someone speaking words for another to write down, so this is the word as spoken

parts.note: illicit means unlawful

explanation.surface: A tyrant uses illegal force to drive someone out.
explanation.walkthrough: The dictator is not a tyrant but one who dictates aloud, so the clue wants a word sounding like ILLICIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out or extract a response, information or reaction from someone.

clue.text: … was banished to former French island and died

parts.note: ex means former
île is French for island
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: Continuing 7: Napoleon was sent away to an island and died there.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exiled means being sent away from one's homeland as a punishment, as Napoleon was.

clue.text: 7 for 1

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., as in ... whist, is a card game, the answer to 7
second meaning: performed by one person alone

explanation.walkthrough: The bare numbers look like arithmetic; 7 points to the answer at 7 Across, and 1 is just one person.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo whist is a card game, and a solo performance is done by a single individual.

clue.text: "Retro" plate way off mark initially for Blair's book

indicators.note: retro means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer
far means a long way off

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter

parts.note: first letter of mark

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned dish, way off the mark, prompts a review of Tony Blair's memoir.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair is not Tony but Eric Blair, the real name of George Orwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's 1945 allegorical novella about farmyard creatures was written under his pen name by Eric Blair.

clue.text: Hosts premiere of movie surrounded by stars

indicators.note: something surrounded by another sits inside it

parts.note: Aries is a constellation, a group of stars

indicators.note: the premiere is the first showing, so take the first letter

parts.note: first letter of movie

explanation.surface: Presenters of a film's first night are mobbed by celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hosts' suggests people who present, but in the old sense a host is a great multitude or army.
explanation.definitionFit: A host in its biblical sense is a large army, so the plural means military forces.

clue.text: … last trio of urchins tearfully getting thinner and thinner

indicators.note: the last trio means the final three letters only

parts.note: the last three letters of urchins
weeping describes someone tearful

explanation.surface: Continuing 8: street children crying as they grow ever skinnier.
explanation.definitionFit: Insweeping describes a curve that narrows inwards, tapering progressively like a shape getting narrower.

clue.text: Supreme pimp exposed American in danger

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: pimp with its outer letters gone

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: peril means danger

explanation.surface: A top pimp lays bare an American who is at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial means relating to an emperor, hence sovereign and supreme in power and authority.

clue.text: Flash barge for city on river

parts.note: a flash is a moment, informally a mo
a scow is a flat-bottomed barge

explanation.surface: A showy barge is heading for a riverside city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' looks like an adjective meaning showy, but it is a noun: an instant. The city stands on the Moskva, and Napoleon famously retreated from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian capital is built on the Moskva river, which shares its name.

clue.text: Astonished second in command went to capture Marshal

indicators.note: second in means take the second letter of the next word

parts.note: the second letter of command

indicators.note: capturing something holds it inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: went, in the toilet sense, means peed
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: A deputy commander went off to seize a marshal and was amazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second in command' reads as a deputy, but it means the second letter of command. 'Went' has its lavatorial sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wide-eyed with surprise is amazed, staring with eyes fully open in wonder.

clue.text: Gold coins in circulation more than once

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
bits are small coins

explanation.surface: Gold coins have been passed around repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in circulation' suggests money being spent, but it means going round and round repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbits are repeated revolutions around a body, so going round several times describes them.

clue.text: Good man, very tired, hugging old mater?

definitions.note: a playful noun: one who mates, as a breeding stud does

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a good man

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping around, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: all in means exhausted

explanation.surface: A saintly, exhausted man embraces his elderly mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mater' looks like the Latin-derived word for mother; the question mark flags a coinage meaning one who mates.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse kept for breeding is put to mares, so it is one that mates.

clue.text: Tropical fruit puds

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the papaya, a fruit of hot climates
second meaning, playfully: a pud is a nursery word for a paw or hand

explanation.surface: Desserts made with exotic fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puds' looks like British slang for puddings (desserts), but pud is also a nursery word for a hand or paw.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaya, an orange-fleshed fruit of the tropics, is also called by this doubled name.

clue.text: Island where the lanes are windy?

indicators.note: windy roads twist about, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which island has winding lanes.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the South Atlantic island where Napoleon spent his final exile.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Helena is a remote British territory in the South Atlantic, an isolated volcanic isle.

clue.text: Top horse failing to finish in races

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy, the Isle of Man motorcycle races

indicators.note: failing to finish means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a shire is a heavy draught horse

explanation.surface: A leading horse fails to complete its races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like first place in a race but is a garment worn on the upper body.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual short-sleeved garment for the upper body is commonly called a top.

clue.text: Do talk on radio? This could be fine

indicators.note: on the radio you only hear the words, so this is the sound of them

parts.note: to do someone is to con them; yak is slang for talk

explanation.surface: A question about whether chatting on air would be all right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like 'all right', but fine is a grade of brandy, as in fine champagne cognac.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine is a quality grading for French brandy, so a bottle from the Charente could be a fine.

clue.text: One taking orders / put on a show

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a clergyman assistant, having taken holy orders
second meaning: to organise and select works for an exhibition

explanation.walkthrough: 'taking orders' suggests a waiter, but holy orders are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant parish priest has entered holy orders, and a museum organiser selects exhibits for display.

clue.text: Merchant Seaman, say, pursuing quiet work

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so this piece follows the others

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
op is short for opus, a work
David Seaman was England's goalkeeper, an example of a keeper

explanation.surface: A merchant sailor following quiet work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merchant Seaman' reads as one phrase about a sailor; Seaman is the footballer David Seaman, a goalkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer who runs a store is a trader, which is what a merchant is.

clue.text: Banker's not entirely penniless

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the word is used, a run of letters inside it

parts.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: A bank employee is close to broke.
explanation.walkthrough: A banker in crosswords is often a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A river has banks, so it is jokingly a banker; this is the Egyptian waterway.

clue.text: Reject metal wrapper used in Japanese eatery

indicators.note: to reject is to turn back, so the word is turned around

parts.note: iron is a metal

explanation.surface: A sushi bar turns away a metal wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Nori is dried seaweed pressed into sheets, rolled around rice in sushi.

clue.text: Country intended to replace Independent with Republican

indicators.note: to replace means one letter is swapped out for another
with names the letter that comes in

parts.note: a fiancé is one's intended, the person one plans to marry

explanation.surface: A nation planned to swap independent politicians for republican ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intended' reads as a verb, but it is a noun for a betrothed partner.
explanation.definitionFit: France is a nation of western Europe, and Napoleon's own.

clue.text: At last, action stations!

parts.note: Napoleon's final battle was his last action, and this is also the name of a major London railway station

explanation.walkthrough: 'Action stations' is the call to battle; split it and you get Napoleon's last action plus a London terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's final defeat in 1815 was in Belgium, and a London terminus bears the same name.
